findings.message: The sea scene's drawing of the duel marker (crossed swords and elapsed time) has no test. seaScene.ts publishes data-markers with position and elapsed text, but no unit or e2e test reads it; sea-duel has no third browser. Coverage stops at state delivery (tests/integration/seaDuel.test.ts watcher: marker at the encounter tile, stranger sees none) and the pure elapsedText formatter (apps/web/src/seaDuel.test.ts). The rendering, and whether it uses the marker's position and startTick, could regress unnoticed.
findings.requirement: a duel marker (crossed swords and elapsed time) shows at the encounter position to players in sight

findings.message: 'They stop' is not tested at room level. Every integration grapple that lands (seaDuel.test.ts first test, pairInRange/playersAt) places both ships at rest, so speed 0 and an unchanged position during the reservation would hold even if MatchRoom never stopped a moving ship. Only the pure stopShip helper is tested on a moving ship (simulation.test.ts). The e2e host coasts into the grapple but nothing asserts that its ship stops.
findings.requirement: a hit reserves both ships (they stop and ignore sailing input)

findings.message: The both-not-ready cancel test (seaDuel.test.ts 'cancels the duel when neither fighter is ready in time') asserts only the result ('cancelled', draw protection), not when it happens. The forfeit case checks >= 9.5 s since the grapple. A cancel at the countdown's end instead of 10 s would still pass.
findings.requirement: One client not ready at 10 s forfeits; both not ready cancels.

findings.message: The candidate's integration check took 201.1 s against its 300 s timeout (log-3: 'Duration 201.10s'). That leaves about a third of the budget on a shared machine. The harness was split into seaDuelHarness.test.ts, but the standalone duel.test.ts alone takes 69 s and files largely run in sequence.
findings.requirement: The integration suite stays well inside its 300 s check timeout (split the harness if needed).
